rationale: Both candidates go well beyond the ground truth's fairly light docs/test-marker complaints into real code-level bugs, and both independently converge on several genuine issues (uncached get_kernel() per attention layer, the unwrapped final get_kernel() call with no fallback, FA3-Hub's major>=9 gate wrongly admitting Blackwell) — this convergence lends credibility to both. Y more precisely recalls the ground-truth threads: it directly answers wtomin's 'what do version=1/2/default mean' question with concrete evidence (branch SHAs, actual warning text) rather than just proposing a pin, and it correctly identifies that RuixiangMa's flash_attn_func=None crash concern is only partially fixed (the piecewise path was patched but _forward_varlen_masked/_run_varlen_dense still call an unchecked varlen_func), whereas X marks that whole area '[resolved]' without noticing the masked-path gap still exists. Y's findings are also generally more verifiable/grounded (shows actual timing runs, simulated selector matrix, real repo version metadata) and read as a coherent, well-prioritized human review, while X's is comprehensive but its finding headlines are truncated/garbled ('[…]') and wrapped in denser, harder-to-parse scaffolding. X does add a few plausible unique findings (LTX-2 mask conversion, diffusers-adapter case fallthrough) that Y lacks, keeping the gap from being decisive.
